Same warning was flagged in iter-50 — not introduced by iter-51, not blocking. UI renders all 18 inbox rows + 5 domain rows correctly.

action_items: No functional issues — Phase 1 Infrastructure module is shipping-ready.

Cosmetic-only: the pre-existing motion.tr hydration warning continues to fire on the new Infrastructure tables (and on Drip Campaigns from iter-50). Wrap inbox/domain rows in a plain <tr> (or memo-export a non-instrumented row component) if you want to silence it. Non-blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: infrastructure_routes.py (~453 lines, single file) — clean separation: _domain_of / _emails_sent_today / _compute_status / _load_inboxes / _summarise helpers + build_infrastructure_router. Status mapping is correctly prioritised: Risky (disconnected/last_error) > Warming Up > Paused > Fully Reserved > Partially Available > Available — matches spec.
_load_inboxes pre-builds campaign/drip assignment map in 2 Mongo round-trips total (not N), which scales correctly with workspace growth.

Tenant scoping is explicit (`if not is_admin: q['user_id'] = user_doc['user_id']`) for accounts AND for campaign/drip queries — verified at runtime via Mongo cross-check that non-admin sees only own accounts.
Ownership endpoint deliberately returns 404 (not 403) for non-owner non-admin to avoid leaking account existence — documented behaviour, matches spec.

list_inboxes does an extra unfiltered _load_inboxes call just to build the dropdown options. Cheap today (<100 accounts/tenant) but worth memoising via a single load + two passes if a workspace ever crosses ~1000 accounts. Non-blocking.
/export uses StreamingResponse with iter([content]) and a correct media_type per format. Filename includes UTC date — fine.

Phase-1 estimate `remaining_week = remaining_today * 7` and `remaining_30_days * 30` is intentional + the response includes an explicit `capacity.note` calling it out. UI also tags both with `est.` chips. Not a bug.
infrastructure-permission audit log entry written via audit_log collection (action: infrastructure_permission_updated) — good operational hygiene matching the blog-permission pattern.
/api/auth/me bool coercion (`bool(user_doc.get('can_access_infrastructure', False))`) handles legacy users that never had the field — verified via fresh user returning False.
